explanation: I found no Mathlib declaration that states this result. The theorem says: if p is odd, ζ is a primitive p-th root of unity, and f satisfies f(c⁻¹) = f(c), then the sum of f(ζ^j) over j in [1, p) is twice the sum over k in [1, p/2]. The proof uses two helper lemmas from the library itself, `sum_Ico_eq_sum_half_pair` and `inv_zetaPow`, together with routine rewriting; it calls no Mathlib result that carries the content. I grepped Mathlib for half-range sums of the form `Icc 1 (p / 2)` and `Ico … (p / 2)`. The only hits were in GaussEisensteinLemmas, which work over ZMod p with `valMinAbs` and have nothing to do with sums over powers of a root of unity. I found no general lemma that folds a sum over powers of a root of unity using the symmetry ζ^(p-k) = (ζ^k)⁻¹.
